description: The Global Atlas for Renewable Energy is IRENA's platform for mapping and assessing renewable energy resources anywhere in the world, the core of an initiative launched in 2009 with the Clean Energy Ministerial Multilateral Solar and Wind Working Group. IRENA's May 2024 brochure says it uses an open-source architecture and existing databases to give actionable information on wind speeds, annual solar irradiation, areas available for development, population growth and relationships to grid infrastructure, and that since 2013 it has been updated with inputs from more than 50 research institutions and 39 countries. Around the platform, IRENA built online tools and analyses: zoning assessment for utility-scale solar PV and onshore wind, a bioenergy simulator, pre-feasibility site assessment, the SolarCity simulator and capacity-building workshops, with an annex of data providers. Coverage is global, aimed at countries lacking resource data and expertise. Access: web platform; the page itself returned no text when fetched, so data formats, download routes and terms of the platform are unverified. Caveats: resource datasets come from many providers with differing terms. It suits renewable capacity planning studies, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
